title: Tutorial: Call Your First Module
scenario: A module is a reusable package of Terraform files with inputs and outputs. Calling one is just a module block: a name, a source and the inputs the module expects.
constraints: Create a module block named storage.

focus.title: Complete the module call
focus.todo: Add the module source and pass the bucket name input.

hints.why: Modules are how Terraform code scales beyond a single file. A module call lets you reuse a tested component without copying its resources.
hints.what: Complete the module block so it loads the local storage module and passes the one input that module expects.
hints.when: Use a module when a group of resources is reused or when a team needs a stable interface. A local source is ideal while developing the module in the same repository.
hints.how: Look at the module block labels first. The source argument is a path, so it is a string. The other argument matches an input variable inside the module, so its value is an expression from the root configuration.

test_manifest.title: the module points at the local module
the bucket name is passed into the module
